slides.title: Options Contracts
slides.content: An option is a contract. A 'Call Option' gives you the RIGHT, but not the obligation, to buy 100 shares of a stock at a specific 'Strike Price' by a certain 'Expiration Date'.

slides.title: The Premium
slides.content: You pay a fee (the Premium) to buy this contract. If the stock explodes in value, you can exercise the contract to buy the shares at the cheap strike price!

slides.title: Extreme Leverage
slides.content: Options are incredibly powerful. A $500 option can become worth $5,000 in a day. BUT, if the stock doesn't reach the strike price before it expires, your option becomes worth exactly $0.

quiz.question: What does a Call Option give you?

options.text: The right (but not obligation) to buy shares at a specific price
options.explanation: A call option is a bet that the price will go up.

quiz.question: If your call option expires and the stock price is LOWER than your strike price, what happens?

options.text: You must buy the shares anyway
The option expires worthless and you lose the premium you paid
options.explanation: Out-of-the-money options expire with zero value.
